summary: The optimized online method (raw mid-layer attention at L12 + MIS diversity selection) achieves 66.32% average grounding accuracy across 8 RefCOCO/RefCOCO+/RefCOCOg splits at 10% keep ratio, exceeding D2Pruner (55.03%) by +11.28 points. It retains 92% of no-pruning accuracy while eliminating offline calibration data entirely. The improvement is consistent across all 8 splits (min +9.55, max +13.64).
analysis: Four methods compared on InternVL2.5-8B at 10% keep ratio: No-pruning (72.06%), FastV (33.85%), D2Pruner with offline prior at L2 (55.03%), and our method with raw attention at L12 (66.32%). The success criterion (within 1.0 point of D2Pruner) is far exceeded — our method outperforms D2Pruner by +11.28 points. Per-dataset: RefCOCO +11.06, RefCOCO+ +12.10, RefCOCOg +10.40. The key insight is that deeper pruning layers (L12 vs L2) provide semantically richer attention that makes offline debiasing unnecessary. The original shallow-layer ratio debiasing failed (13.24%), and even at L12 adding shallow prior as weighted combination (64.24%) slightly hurts vs raw attention (66.32%). Phase-0 correctly predicted this: shallow attention is not position-correlated (rho ~0.17).
reason: Verdict is 'good' because: (1) Both main experiment and all baselines completed successfully with full results on all 8 splits. (2) The optimized method substantially surpasses D2Pruner (+11.28 points average, consistent across all splits), far exceeding the -1.0 success threshold. (3) It eliminates offline calibration entirely, a practical advantage. (4) 92% performance retention vs 76.4% for D2Pruner. The caveat is that the gain comes from deeper pruning layers rather than from the shallow-layer debiasing originally hypothesized, but the end result (calibration-free pruning outperforming D2Pruner) is a strong positive signal.
